answer: Bind each voting seat to a state professional licence held by its operator, listed in a public licensing board register under their legal name. One licence backs one seat. Earning one means exams, about $400 in fees and often a year of supervised hours, whether for a welder certified on ferrous pipe or a pilot guiding ships to a wharf. A farm of 200 clones would spend $80,000 and years of work before casting a vote. A lapsed licence becomes a relic and drops its seat.
